dimensions.note: The workflows define and persist no credentials; caller-selected models and Swamp grants own runtime capability and secret boundaries.
Declarative workflows have no custom logger surface; Swamp records assertion, model-method, and nested-workflow lifecycle events.
Unsafe identifiers, incomplete delivery configuration, and repeated outbox identities fail before adapter or enqueue side effects; downstream failures propagate for run resume.

Synthetic runtime evidence covers exact artifact selection, daily digest, failed and completed delivery, replay suppression, disabled delivery, two-item fan-out, malformed configuration, predicate injection, empty batches, and duplicate identities. A Moment Savor swap also verified that incompatible native model protocols are rejected rather than hidden behind opaque mappings.
The evaluator owns durable transition state, unchanged states emit no intent, batch identities are unique, and the notification outbox owns deduplication and retry state.

Transition intents exactly match the notification-outbox contract; model/spec selectors scope every handoff, and the compatibility matrix explicitly distinguishes conforming protocols from incompatible native model schemas.
The workflows open no files or connections and directly create no provider resources.
README, contracts, and examples contain only generic model names, policies, and placeholder values.
